title_original: 2nd Edition of the NARRATIVA – FUJIFILM Award, the winners

blocks.text: The 2nd edition of the NARRATIVA – FUJIFILM Award received 175 submissions, reinforcing the interest in and engagement with this initiative dedicated to contemporary photography in Portugal. Open to artists aged 18 and over, at different stages of their artistic careers, the award recognizes unpublished projects that explore new photographic perspectives and visual languages. The jury, composed of Yael Martinez, Ana Rocha, and Mário Cruz, selected Westernmost, by Bruno Pereira Ribeiro, as the winning project. Two honourable mentions were also awarded: Tatiana Iartseva for Secret Garden and David Henriques for Parque. The selected works represent distinct approaches to image-making, ranging from social essay and documentary photography to authorial research, reflecting the diversity of practices featured in this edition. As part of the award, Bruno Pereira Ribeiro will receive €3,500 and present Westernmost in a solo exhibition at NARRATIVA, in Lisbon, scheduled to open in January 2027. The projects by Tatiana Iartseva and David Henriques will be presented in a public session, also at NARRATIVA, offering audiences the opportunity to discover the works distinguished with an Honourable Mention.

WINNER Bruno Pereira Ribeiro Westernmost The jury distinguished Westernmost, by Bruno Pereira Ribeiro, for the way it transforms the observation of the island of Santo Antão, in Cape Verde, into a reflection on the complexity of territories and the fragility of the boundaries that define them. Starting from a landscape marked by contrasts, the artist challenges seemingly evident spatial divisions, revealing a reality in which the opposition between natural elements gives way to subtle relationships of continuity and transformation. Through a coherent and sensorially expressive visual narrative, Bruno Pereira Ribeiro brings together the materiality of the landscape and the traces of human intervention, constructing an essay that combines documentary observation with conceptual reflection. In this context, the insular and peripheral condition of Santo Antão acquires a meaning that goes beyond geography, raising questions of isolation, permanence, and the relationship between human beings and the environments they inhabit. Through his attention to matter, light, and colour, the photographer explores these tensions without reducing them to immediate interpretations. Westernmost stands out for its ability to construct an open-ended narrative in which images complement and expand one another while preserving the complexity of what they observe. The jury highlights the singularity of Bruno Pereira Ribeiro’s essay and the consistency of an approach that transforms the observation of a territory into a visual experience that lingers beyond the images themselves, inviting a deeper understanding of the relationships between landscape, materiality, and human presence.

HONOURABLE MENTIONS Tatiana Iartseva Secret Garden The jury awarded an Honourable Mention to Secret Garden, by Tatiana Iartseva, for the way it explores, through photography, the relationship between identity and those aspects of human nature that we tend to repress or reject. Placing her own body at the centre of the work, Tatiana Iartseva transforms self-representation into an exercise in experimentation and discovery. Through handcrafted printing techniques incorporating natural elements, she explores the transformation of the figure and its relationship with its surroundings, creating sensorial images that oscillate between presence and disappearance. Secret Garden stands out for its articulation between personal research and experimentation, revealing how the creative process can become a form of knowledge. The jury emphasizes the intimacy of an approach that places the artist’s own experience at the foundation of the photographic investigation, transforming vulnerability into a possibility for recognition and transformation.

David Henriques Parque The jury awarded an Honourable Mention to Parque, by David Henriques, for the way it addresses the contradictions of a territory deeply shaped by tourism, taking as its starting point the residential complex where the author lives and which has been part of his family’s history for several generations. In a space that functions simultaneously as a permanent residence and temporary accommodation, the photographer finds a place where different ways of inhabiting and experiencing space intersect. Drawing on this biographical relationship with the location, David Henriques constructs a visual narrative that combines proximity and distance. His direct knowledge of the place does not prevent a critical perspective on its contradictions; rather, it allows him to observe how the transformation of the Algarve is reflected in a territory that is simultaneously familiar and deprived of clear markers of identity. The photographs reveal an environment shaped to meet the expectations of tourism, where architectural repetition and spatial organization seem to suspend the cultural particularities of the place, without erasing the traces of everyday life that persist beyond its tourist function. The jury highlights the creation of a subtle and consistent narrative that begins with a personal experience to question a collective reality.
